author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I am willing to let the KPI definition remain missing for this release. The physical stock is already committed to the supplier, and the trucks leave next week. We need to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders. If the acceptance criteria are automated, I can accept the lack of a formal KPI definition. The risk of delay outweighs the benefit of a complete metric right now. We can backfill the definition once the system is stable and the immediate pressure of the promotion week has passed. This trade allows us to meet the deadline while keeping the logic auditable through automation.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept the loss of a formal KPI definition in exchange for meeting the immediate shipping deadline, prioritizing speed over completeness.
